name: implement
description: Implement one settled GitHub ticket through TDD, observed verification, and committed code review.
adaptations: Use connected GitHub feature branches and commits as Equivalent Mechanisms while protecting the default branch from implicit mutation.
Load tdd only at the upstream testing point and keep both tdd and code-review as separate Dependency Skills rather than embedding their runtimes.
Treat typecheck, test, and commit outcomes as observed only after their live results are returned; report unavailable verification or mutation capability instead of inventing a result.
Quarantine the pinned review-before-commit contradiction as the Temporary Upstream Fix documented in docs/adr/implement-review-order.md.

changeRecords.evidence: The Target Runtime Profile writes through connected GitHub APIs, whose file-write operations can target the default branch when no branch is supplied. Selecting a non-default feature branch before production mutations preserves the upstream implementation step without implicit default-branch mutation. Recording the pre-implementation head supplies the fixed point required by the separately loaded code-review dependency.

transform.match: Implement the work described by the user in the spec or tickets.
transform.replacement: Implement the work described by the user in the spec or tickets. Through connected GitHub, resolve the intended base and any existing feature branch. If the work is not already on an explicitly selected non-default branch, create a feature branch from the intended base before production mutations. Do not mutate the repository default branch unless the upstream workflow and an explicit user instruction authorize that direct mutation; if the required branch or GitHub write capability is unavailable, stop the affected mutation and report it as incomplete. Before changing production code, record the current feature-branch head as `review_base` and keep that fixed point unchanged for the later `code-review` invocation.

changeRecords.evidence: The Target Runtime Profile loads Dependency Skills through the MCP load_skill tool. This changes only the invocation mechanism at the exact upstream testing point.

transform.match: Use /tdd where possible, at pre-agreed seams.
transform.replacement: Use `tdd` with `load_skill` where possible, at pre-agreed seams.

changeRecords.evidence: The Target Runtime Profile may use connected CI or another live runner rather than a local shell. Naming that Equivalent Mechanism and requiring its returned result preserves the upstream typecheck and test cadence without inventing additional verification steps.

transform.match: Run typechecking regularly, single test files regularly, and the full test suite once at the end.
transform.replacement: Run typechecking regularly, single test files regularly, and the full test suite once at the end through an available live execution mechanism. Treat each run as complete only after observing its returned result; if no live execution mechanism is available, report that verification step as unobserved.

changeRecords.evidence: The Target Runtime Profile commits through connected GitHub rather than an assumed local git executable. Naming that Equivalent Mechanism and requiring the returned commit result preserves the upstream commit operation without adding publication or verification steps.

transform.match: Commit your work to the current branch.
transform.replacement: Commit your work to the current feature branch through connected GitHub. Treat the commit as complete only after observing its returned result; if GitHub write capability is unavailable, stop the commit operation and report it as incomplete.

transform.match: Once done, use /code-review to review the work.
transform.replacement: Once done, first commit the verified implementation to the current feature branch through connected GitHub and observe the returned commit result, then load `code-review` with `load_skill` and review the committed diff from the recorded `review_base` to that implementation commit. Continue with the upstream commit step for any work remaining after review.
